analysis: Examined .github/workflows/ci.yml base lines 529-893 and head lines 1-537. The visible head change is CI-only. It adds SAVE_CACHES, which is true only for pushes to master or dev, and a sparse-checkout setting. Each job also gains a .git cache sequence: restore, discard on git fsck failure, checkout with persist-credentials: false, and save only when SAVE_CACHES is true. Actions are pinned by SHA and permissions stay contents: read. No secrets, release signing, attestation, coordinator protocol or provider runtime code changed, so I found no regression against the retained provider threat model (T-041, T-053, T-054, A-017). Pull requests only restore caches and never save them, so a PR cannot poison the master or dev .git cache. A restored .git is checked only for HEAD and connectivity by `git fsck --connectivity-only`. It is not checked for config, hooks or other non-object files. Safety therefore depends on only trusted pushes writing the cache, which the visible SAVE_CACHES gating enforces. Coverage limits: head changed ranges extend to about line 1157, but only head lines 1-537 were supplied, and the patch excerpt is truncated. The later jobs (cluster, focused, gate, and head lines 664-1157) were not visible on the head side. Another pass should confirm that those jobs use the same restore-only .git cache on PRs and that provider-test-gate still requires the same job results. The release and signing workflows are out of scope for this batch.
